kongres-i-1960.title: Congress I
kongres-i-1960.summary: The first Congress, the adoption of the name Gereja Gerakan Pentakosta and its emblem, and the appointment of central leaders.
blocks: The first Congress of Gereja Penggerakan Kristus was held on 05–08 April 1960 at Gereja Kristus, Sindanglaya, Cipanas, West Java. The Congress recognized that the church as an institution was already acknowledged and protected by the government under the Staatsblad (State Gazette) of 1917, and that turning it into a foundation or placing it under one was a mistake. The growing number of congregations also made a better organizational structure necessary to meet the needs of the time.
The Congress ultimately resolved to:
1. Change the name Gereja Penggerakan Kristus to Gereja Gerakan Pentakosta (GGP).
2. Adopt the GGP emblem, consisting of the Bible, a cross, a tongue of fire, and a crown.
3. Ratify the Articles of Association and Bylaws.
4. Establish Gereja Gerakan Pentakosta (GGP) as a legal entity under the Staatsblad, no longer under Yayasan Penggerakan Kristus.
5. Appoint Pdt. MPT Kandou as Chairperson, with the following central leadership:
Chairperson : Pdt. MPT Kandou
Chairperson I : Pdt. Jap Jo Keng Hong
Chairperson II : Pdt. Laurens Sumaraw
Secretary: Pdt. J.H.Hukom
Deputy Secretary : Pdt. Gayus Suwuh
Treasurer : Bpk. Tan Liang Hoey
and members
6. Authorize the Central Council to appoint and confer the title of pastor.

The election of the Chairperson and other officers was conducted openly in a spirit of Christian fellowship. After Congress I, GGP adopted a congregational-synodal structure: congregations remained autonomous while jointly agreeing to a central leadership based in Jakarta.
7. Yayasan Penggerakkan Kristus was not, or had not yet been, dissolved. Its principal task was limited to maintaining and protecting land and church buildings.

kongres-ii-1964.title: Congress II
kongres-ii-1964.summary: The formation of the Spiritual Council, the 1964–1968 leadership, and the early development of GGP's youth organization.
blocks: Congress II took place on 3–8 February 1964 in Langowan, North Sulawesi, with the theme: ‘Be holy, for I, the Lord your God, am holy’ (Leviticus 9:2b, as cited in the source).
Several resolutions of Congress II:
(1) Amend several articles of the Articles of Association and Bylaws.
(2) Approve the proposal for GGP to apply for membership in the Indonesian Council of Churches (DGI).
(3) Establish a Spiritual Council (DR) comprising:
1. Pdt. Laurens Sumaraw
2. Pdt. MPT Kandou
3. Pdt. Jan David Jaquet
4. Pdt. Hendrik P Sinjal
The Spiritual Council's task: advise on spiritual matters that the Central Council cannot resolve.
(4). Elect and appoint the following Central Council leadership for 1964–1968:
Chairperson I : Pdt. The Kim Jan Hendrik (John H.Thera)
Chairperson II : Pdt. Arnold Kumolontang
Chairperson III : Pdt. Jap Jo Keng Hong
Secretary : Pdt. Jordan H.Hukom
Treasurer : Bpk. Tan Liang Hoey
The election was conducted orally/by acclamation. Congress II showed an emerging awareness of the need to learn better organizational practices.

In 1966, Pdt. The Kim Jan H resigned as Chairperson I at the Central Supplementary Assembly in Cipanas, Sindanglaya, West Java. In August 1965, GGP's young people had held their first Youth Congress at Gereja Kristus Sindanglaya Cipanas, West Java. The Congress established Persatuan Pemuda Gereja Gerakan Pentakosta (PPGGP), ratified its regulations, and appointed the following PPGGP leadership:

Treasurer : Sdri. Ivonne Makaminan
Member : 1. Sdr Khoe Sen Tjew (Daniel Sukendra)

sidang-raya-iv-1972.title: General Assembly IV
sidang-raya-iv-1972.summary: The assembly at Wisma Oikoumene, the 1972–1976 leadership, and the appointment of GGP's Spiritual Father.
blocks: GGP General Assembly IV was held on 25–29 July 1972 at Wisma Oikoumene DGI in Sukabumi, West Java, with the theme: ‘Be filled with the Holy Spirit’ (Ephesians 5:18).

The lead-up to General Assembly IV did not go as expected; organizational tensions were strongly felt and persisted into the proceedings. Many regional delegates were uncomfortable with these dynamics and, unable to understand them, chose to walk out before the assembly ended. Rev. Hendrik Thiessen, who was present, sought to calm the situation and eventually eased the tensions.
The following Central Council officers for 1972–1976 were ultimately elected orally (mondeling) and by acclamation:
Chairperson I : Pdt. Arnold Kumolontang
Chairperson II : Pdt. Junus Hanan(Jap Jo Keng Hong)
Secretary I : Pdt. O.Ch.J.S.Wohon
Secretary II : Pdt. Md Soep Soegiardjo
Treasurer : Ibu Annie Makaminan-Mohede General Assistant : Pdt. John H Sumaraw
Pdt. S.Todingpadang
Pdm. Els Jedidjah Harun
Pdm. Ernest Kereh
Several resolutions of General Assembly IV/1972 included:
(1) The assembly agreed to appoint Pdt. Hendrik Thiessen as GGP's Spiritual Father.
(2) Pdt. Arnold Kumolontang, as Chairperson I, was required to move to Jakarta, where the Central Council office was based.

sidang-raya-v-1976.title: General Assembly V
sidang-raya-v-1976.summary: The author's account of proceedings in Bongkudai Baru and the Central Council leadership for 1976–1980.
blocks: The General Assembly returned to North Sulawesi, this time to GGP Bongkudai Baru in Bolaang Mongondow regency.
The following are notes by the author, Pdp. Daniel Sukendra, who attended as a youth delegate:

1. GGP Bongkudai Baru had been founded and was pastored by Pdt. Hein Mangribeth. Its church building was fairly large but very simple, made of timber and boards. This cool, quiet area had no electricity, so pressurized kerosene lamps provided light at dusk and at night.
2. Delegates were accommodated in congregation members' homes.
3. Once again, preparations appeared minimal and facilities below the standard expected for a national assembly.
4. The atmosphere before the proceedings was still affected by the ‘trauma’ of General Assembly IV in 1972.
5. The two ‘rival’ groups from North Sulawesi each prepared to ‘take power’, while the incumbents sought to ‘retain power’ over the Central Council leadership.
6. Most participants or delegates came from North Sulawesi. Very few came from Java because of limited funds for transport.
7. As at earlier assemblies, the Central Council was not yet familiar with establishing a quorum and rules of procedure.
8. The prevailing mood at General Assembly V differed little from that at General Assembly IV/1972 in Sukabumi.
The General Assembly seemed focused solely on electing the Central Council Chairperson.
• Proceedings took place under these circumstances, and the outcome was fairly predictable.

Comments, proposals, and suggestions from delegates, especially those from Java, were not properly accommodated. As at previous General Assemblies, proceedings were chaired directly by the Central Executive Council (MHP).

• Shortly before the election of the Central Council Chairperson, delegates from Jakarta and West Java walked out, frustrated that the assembly leadership had not accommodated their comments, suggestions, and proposals.
Seeing this, Pdt. H. Thiessen intervened as Spiritual Father and brought reassurance to those who had walked out.
• The Central Council Chairperson was again elected orally/by acclamation, and Pdt. Arnold Kumolontang was re-elected for a third term.
• The Central Council for 1976–1980 was as follows:
Chairperson I : Pdt. Arnold Kumolontang
Chairperson II: (temporarily vacant)
Secretary I : Pdt. Md Arnan Hely Marshali (Lie Koen Gie)
Secretary II : Pdt. Md Jantje Kojongian
Treasurer : Ibu. Annie Makaminan-Mohede
Member : 1. Pdt. John H Sumaraw
2. Pdt. S.Todingpadang BA
3. Pdt. Ernest Kereh
4. Pdt. Els Jedidjah Harun
5. Pdt. Md Hizkia Soewignjo
6. Pb. Pdt. Daniel Sukendra BA
• At a Central Council meeting after General Assembly V, Pdt. Jusak Jonathan was appointed Chairperson II, as Pdt. Junus Hanan had passed away shortly after attending the assembly.

• Author's note: During GGP's 16 years of organizational life, from Assembly I (1960) to Assembly V (1976), results could be described as falling short of expectations because leadership capacity was inadequate.

sidang-pelengkap-1978.title: Central Supplementary Assembly
sidang-pelengkap-1978.summary: Central Council appointments and preparations for General Assembly VI in 1980.
blocks: Two years after General Assembly V, a Central Supplementary Assembly was held in Mega Mendung, West Java, on 03–06 July 1978.
Before that assembly, Central Council Secretary I, Pdt. Md Arnan H Marshali, suffered a stroke and a prolonged illness that prevented him from carrying out his duties.

Pdt. Md Jantje Kojongian then assumed the duties of Secretary I. However, relations between Chairperson I and the acting Secretary I were strained, especially during preparations for the Central Supplementary Assembly, leaving the Central Executive Council's work effectively at a standstill.

In response, Treasurer Ibu. Annie Makaminan took the initiative to involve Pb. Pdt. Daniel Sukendra, a Central Council assistant member, in preparing the assembly. Central Council Chairperson I, Pdt. Arnold Kumolontang, welcomed the initiative.
Recognizing that management had been a weakness in the Central Council's organization, LPMI Director Drs. Agus Lay was invited to give a talk on church management.

The Supplementary Assembly ultimately proceeded smoothly. Both groups from North Sulawesi unanimously asked Pb. Pdt. Daniel Sukendra to fill the vacancy as acting Central Council Secretary I. The vacant Chairperson II position was also filled, resulting in the following leadership:
Chairperson I : Pdt. Arnold Kumolontang
Chairperson II : Pdt. Jusak Jonathan
Acting Secretary I : Pb. Pdt. Daniel Sukendra
Secretary II : Pdt. Jantje Kojongian
Treasurer : Ibu. Annie Makaminan-Mohede
Members : 1. Pdt. J.H.Sumaraw
2. Pdt. S.Todingpadang BA
3. Pdt Ernest Kereh
4. Pdm. Hizkia Soewignyo
5. Pdm. Els Jedidja Harun
Several notes:
1. In 1979, the Central Executive Council sent Pdt. Abraham Gunawan to establish a Bible school.

2. The Central Executive Council also sent Pdt. Ernest Kereh to inaugurate the GGP congregation in Nunukan, North Kalimantan, in Bongkudai Baru, later continued by Pdt. Hizkia Soewignyo. This Bible school became the forerunner of STTP in Mooat. [The wording and sequence follow the source.]

3. A year before General Assembly VI, Pdt. Arnold Kumolontang passed away on 13 December 1979. Preparations were undertaken by the Central Executive Council then in office: Pb. Pdt. Daniel Sukendra, Pdm. Jantje Kojongian, Pdt. Jusak Jonathan, and Ibu. Annie Makaminan-Mohede, together with the active West Java Regional Council Secretary, Pdt. Md Toemiran, who also chaired the organizing committee.

sidang-raya-vi-1980.title: General Assembly VI
sidang-raya-vi-1980.summary: A generational transition, renewed assembly procedures, and Central Council ministry programs for 1980–1984.
blocks: General Assembly VI was held at Bina Warga, Cipayung, West Java, from 31 August to 05 September 1980, with the theme: ‘Jesus Christ makes all things new’ (Revelation 21:5).

The theme was accepted following a proposal by Pdp. Daniel Sukendra, who was concerned about GGP's condition, particularly the unresolved polarization among its ministers in North Sulawesi. Through this theme, all participants were invited to leave the past behind, renew their shared life, and consider a better future for GGP.

Drawing on his experience attending the Indonesian Council of Churches assemblies in Salatiga in 1976 and Tomohon in 1980 with Pdm. Md Toemiran, Daniel Sukendra sought to prepare the schedule and materials for General Assembly VI as carefully as possible. He reworked organizational governance in line with sound principles and norms for church institutions. Through the Central Executive Council, this was the first GGP General Assembly to invite speakers from outside GGP, including Pdt., Dr., SAE Nababan (DGI General Secretary), Pdt. Graham Robert of I-3, Batu Malang, and Pdt. Maitimoe (DGI Oikoumene Institute).
Documentation in Benih yang Tumbuh, page 149.

Decisions were made in plenary sessions, while materials were discussed in sections, actively involving all participants in joint decision-making. At earlier assemblies, discussions and decisions had taken place through ‘brainstorming’ in plenary sessions.
For the first time, the Central Council Chairperson, Secretary, and Treasurer were elected through a direct, free, and secret ballot. The following were democratically elected:

For the first time, through General Assembly VI, GGP entrusted its leadership to a younger generation. Pdt., Ir., P Sinengko was then 36 years old, and Pb. Pdt. Daniel Sukendra was 38.

General Assembly VI in 1980 brought a natural generational transition in GGP leadership alongside reform and renewal of organizational life. Enthusiasm for GGP's calling was rekindled. For the first time, the Central Council had a master plan, prepared by Pdm. Almon Retika as Chairperson of the BINDIK Commission, which became a framework for its programs. The relevant commissions implemented the work program despite severe financial constraints; MP-GGP still depended on contributions from partners in Germany and the Netherlands through the Spiritual Father.

sidang-raya-vii-1984.title: General Assembly VII
sidang-raya-vii-1984.summary: Ministry growth, partner church relationships, and a documentary account of Pdt. Henk Thiessen's life.
blocks: GGP General Assembly VII was held in 1984 at the GSJA Bible school campus in Karanglo, Malang, East Java, with the theme: ‘Grow in every way into Christ’ (Ephesians 4:15). The theme reminded participants to mature in faith and in the true knowledge of Jesus Christ as Head of the Church. Since 1980, GGP had grown significantly, with many new congregations in Java, North Sulawesi, and elsewhere. The Central Executive Council had begun outreach to North Sumatra and transmigration areas in South Lampung. The theme emphasized that congregational growth must be directed toward Christ. The East Java GGP Area Council was appointed to organize the assembly, with Pdt. John Massie as committee chairperson.

The assembly followed the TT/TTG provisions revised at General Assembly VI in 1980, making that constitution the basis of organizational procedure. Proceedings followed rules approved at the opening plenary session. Sections, a Structure Committee, and a Nominations Committee were established. At the first plenary session, five delegates were appointed as the presiding council, with the Central Council Secretary attending as a resource person.

The Central Council presented its accountability report through Secretary Pdt. Md Daniel Sukendra. Participants took part in decision-making through section and committee sessions. As at previous assemblies, Pdt. Hendrik Thiessen attended as GGP's Spiritual Father and offered spiritual counsel. General Assembly VII proceeded well and produced resolutions for the Central Council and all GGP congregations to implement over the following four years. As in 1980, delegates democratically elected a Chairperson, Secretary, and Treasurer by majority vote.
Chairperson : Pdt. Ir Paulus Sinengko
Secretary : Pdt. Md Daniel Sukendra
Treasurer : Ibu. Annie Makaminan-Mohede.

In September 1986, for the first time in GGP's history, Central Council Chairperson Pdt. P.Sinengko and Secretary Pdt. Md Daniel Sukendra were invited by partner CGV in West Germany to attend the Hauptbrudertag assembly at Heimstatte Niedenstein. They also visited several CGV congregations to introduce GGP and its mission work in Indonesia.

Following the visit, CGV partners donated a Toyota Kijang vehicle to STTP in Mooat and a motorcycle to Pdt. Juara Sinaga, pastor of GGP Sidikalang. This followed slide presentations by Central Council Secretary Daniel Sukendra during visits to CGV congregations.

The following achievements of the GGP Central Council over two consecutive terms (1980–1988) are recorded:
1. Establishing and inaugurating several GGP congregations in Palas district, South Lampung (Southern Sumatra).
2. Publishing Hujan Akhir magazine as a means of communication and information.
3. Preparing and publishing GGP's Principles of Doctrine in 1985, the first written doctrinal handbook in GGP's history.
4. Establishing and inaugurating STTP in Mooat, Bolaang Mongondow, in 1985.
5. Strengthening partnerships with CGV (Christlicher Gemeinschaeft Verband an de Ruhr) in West Germany and Pinksterbeweging in the Netherlands.
6. Publishing a GGP worship guide.
7. Planting and establishing new congregations in West Java, Central Java, East Java, Bali, North Sumatra, West Kalimantan, East Kalimantan, and Tana Toraja.
8. Empowering youth, Sunday School, and women's ministries by forming organizations to strengthen their participation in service (the founding meeting was held in Malang).
9. Establishing Yayasan Pelayanan Kasih to support the welfare of ministers serving in remote and rural areas.
10. Working with the government, specifically the Directorate General of Christian Community Guidance and BP-7 DKI Jakarta, to hold a 45-hour P-4 training program in 1984.
11. Strengthening relationships and cooperation with national church organizations such as DGI, PGLII, and PGPI.
Documentation in Benih yang Tumbuh, page 156.
A meeting in Bogor to discuss revisions to GGP's Principles of Doctrine (1989)

Special note: Before General Assembly VIII, GGP's Spiritual Father, Pdt. Hendrik Thiessen, was called home to the Father's eternal dwelling on 11 May 1987 and buried at Pandu Public Cemetery, Bandung. His passing left GGP without a role model in church and organizational life.
Documentation in Benih yang Tumbuh, page 157.

Pdt Hendrik ‘Henk’ Thiessen, GGP's Spiritual Father. Born in Pekantan (North Sumatra) on 28 March 1908; the third of Papa Thiessen's six children. He studied theology at Elim Bible College, London. He married Adriana Wetters; they had no children. After Papa Thiessen passed away in 1953, Henk Thiessen assumed his ministry responsibilities. He served GGP as pastor and evangelist for more than 50 years. He was appointed Spiritual Father at the 1972 GGP General Assembly and passed away in Jakarta on 11 May 1987.

sidang-raya-ix-1992.title: General Assembly IX
sidang-raya-ix-1992.summary: The assembly at Wisma Kinasih, the Minister of Religious Affairs' attendance, and the 1992–1996 leadership.
blocks: Learning from the experience of General Assembly VIII's venue, the Central Executive Council chose Wisma Kinasih in Caringin, Bogor, for General Assembly IX. An organizing committee was formed under Pdm. Suprihatin AM. The theme was: ‘Work while it is still day’ (John 9:5, as cited in the source).
Several notes:

• Wisma Kinasih provided a supportive setting for General Assembly IX, with cool air and comfortable accommodation. A two-day pre-assembly Women's General Meeting (PRW) had taken place at the same venue.

• For the first time, the Central Executive Council successfully invited Indonesia's Minister of Religious Affairs, Bpk. Syadzali, following an audience at the ministry accompanied by Director General of Christian Community Guidance Bpk., Drs., Jan Kawatu. The minister formally opened General Assembly IX and delivered an address. This deserves a place in GGP's history as the first attendance by the Minister of Religious Affairs at a GGP General Assembly.

sidang-raya-x-1996.title: General Assembly X
sidang-raya-x-1996.summary: Proceedings at Grand Hotel Lembang and changes to terms of office and leadership for 1996–2001.
blocks: General Assembly X was held on 08–13 July 1996 at Grand Hotel Lembang, Bandung, West Java. Its organizing committee was chaired by Pdt. Benjamin Soetedjo, Secretary of GGP Shalom, Bandung. The theme was: ‘Keep working while it is still day’ (John 9:4). GGP Shalom made a substantial contribution to this assembly.
Documentation in Benih yang Tumbuh, page 166.
An audience with the late Bpk. Drs., Radius Prawiro at his residence

From left: Bpk. Rhonny Kumontoy; the late Pdm. Suprihatin A.M; the late Drs. Radius Prawiro; the late Pdt., Prof., Drs., John Rompas presenting an assembly souvenir to the late Drs. Radius Prawiro.
Several notes:
• Attendees included the Director General of Christian Community Guidance, MPH-PGI General Secretary Pdt., Dr., J. Patiasina, and other guests from outside GGP.

• The Central Executive Council invited Pdt. Dr Sularso Sopater to speak on globalization. PGI Advisory Council Chairperson Drs., Radius Prawiro, a former Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs, also gave a talk.
• Amendments to TG/TTG included changing the MP-GGP term of office from four years to five.

• The assembly's purpose began shifting from a celebration of faith toward a contest for the General Chairperson's position, affecting the atmosphere of fellowship. Proceedings were fairly constructive from beginning to end. The election system changed: delegates elected only the General Chairperson, who was then mandated to complete the Central Council leadership.
• Pdt. Almon M Retika received the most votes, was elected General Chairperson for a second term, and was mandated to appoint the full Central Council.
Pdt. Almon Retika was then pressured by an ambitious party insisting on also joining the selection team. The resulting Central Council leadership for 1996–2001 was as follows:
General Chairperson : Pdt. Almon M Retika
General Secretary : Pdt., Ir., Paulus Sinengko
Deputy General Secretary : Pdt. Daniel Sukendra
General Treasurer: Bpk. Rhonny Kumontoy, and so on.
The incident described above was regrettable because it disrupted fellowship within GGP, with repercussions continuing into General Assembly XI in 2001.
• Before the Supplementary Assembly, a reshuffle took place and Pdt. Daniel Sukendra was appointed Central Council General Secretary.

• During Pdt. Almon Retika's leadership, GGP Shalom provided considerable financial support for Central Council programs, including regional visits, land/house purchases for GGP in Bandar Lampung, construction of the STTP Mooat campus, and evangelism programs in West Kalimantan, Upper Mahakam, and elsewhere.

sidang-raya-xi-2001.title: General Assembly XI
sidang-raya-xi-2001.summary: The vision of becoming the Church Christ desires, leadership for 2001–2006, and accounts of organizational life in that period.
blocks: General Assembly XI was held at Hotel Purnama, Batu-Malang, East Java. The Central Executive Council appointed the East Java GGP Area Council as host. The organizing committee was chaired by Pdt. Hizkia Soewignyo., S.Th, supported by all GGP congregations in East Java. Its theme was: ‘Do not quench the Spirit’ (1 Thessalonians 5:9, as cited in the source).

Several notes:

a. The venue and operational arrangements for General Assembly XI at Hotel Purnama, Batu-Malang, deserve appreciation, especially the work of the East Java GGP Area Council as host, supported by all congregations

b. of GGP and the organizing committee led by Pdt. Hizkia Soewignyo. After this substantial assembly, the committee handed over a balance of approximately Rp. 26 million, providing initial funds for the newly elected Central Council.

c. Anticipation of a Central Council leadership transition was already evident before the assembly, as Pdt. Almon Retika had served two terms as General Chairperson and could not be re-elected under TTG rules.
d. Competition between prospective General Chairperson candidates was unseemly. Supporters formed factions, as commonly happens in secular organizations.

e. The election retained the democratic system used at the assemblies of 1980, 1984, 1992, and 1996: delegates voted for a General Chairperson, General Secretary, and General Treasurer. The results were:
General Chairperson : Pdt. Nico Kojongian., S.Th., MA
General Secretary : Pdt. Daniel Sukendra

For the first time, GGP formulated and adopted its vision: ‘To become the Church Christ desires.’ For Pdt. Nico Kojongian, his prayer and desire to become Central Council General Chairperson since the 1976 assembly had been fulfilled. Immediately after the assembly, Pdt. Nico returned to Manado for approximately six months to prepare his move to Jakarta, leaving a leadership ‘vacuum’ at the Central Council during that time.

Amid the social dynamics following General Assembly XI, General Chairperson Pdt. Nico K unexpectedly suffered a mild stroke at a meeting in Lembang, Bandung, and was hospitalized there. Central Council work then effectively stagnated for some time. At Bpk. Rhonny Kumontoy's initiative, GGP Ecclesia Christi hosted a meeting with several Regional Council Chairpersons, producing the ‘Kramat Soka Agreement’. The meeting was informal and not provided for in GGP's constitution, TD/TTG; hence the term ‘Agreement’, or a form of memorandum of understanding. In early May 2004, CGV partner church leader Pastor Ekkehart Vetter invited the General Chairperson and General Secretary to visit CGV congregations and attend its annual Hauptbrudertag assembly. CGV later became MV (Muelheimer Verband a.d.Ruhr).
Documentation in Benih yang Tumbuh, page 173.
A visit to the CGV congregation in Bilefeld in May 2004

After the Kramat Soka Agreement and the visit to CGV in Germany, relations among Central Executive Council members, particularly the General Chairperson, General Secretary, and General Treasurer, gradually improved as they sought to improve the Central Council's work.

At the Central Supplementary Assembly in July 2004, the author describes a ‘conspiracy’ by several individuals with an agenda to divide the Central Executive Council, using the Kramat Soka Agreement and slander to remove the General Secretary. The effort succeeded in impeaching the General Secretary, who had been elected in 2001 with more than 70% of the vote. Pdt. Andreas Gunawan was then appointed acting General Secretary, and Pdt. Henky Benaya acting BINDIK Commission Chairperson. In the author's assessment, these individuals had violated TTG provisions and harmed fellowship. The incident led to a continuing leadership crisis and organizational decline, with consequences reaching General Assembly XII in 2006, XIII in 2010, XIV in 2015, and XV in 2021.

Some congregational, area, and regional leaders felt that politics aimed at seizing power had begun to permeate GGP's organizational life. Without realizing it, the organization had become an end in itself rather than a means of fulfilling GGP's calling and task. Note: The Central Council's 2001–2006 term produced scarcely any adequate results, in the author's assessment.

Other assembly resolutions included:

sidang-raya-xv-2021.title: General Assembly XV
sidang-raya-xv-2021.summary: The hybrid assembly in October 2021 and the MP, DP, and BPP leadership for 2021–2026.
blocks: A. Before General Assembly XV

1. Before General Assembly XV, TPCP-GGP received three prospective General Chairperson candidates for 2021–2026: Pdt. Dr. Welly Mamusung, M.Mis (the incumbent, nominated by the North Sulawesi Regional Council); Pdt. Dr., Natanel Sunarno., M.Th (Chairperson 3 of the 2015–2020 Central Council, nominated by the DKI Jakarta Regional Council); and Pdt. Dicky Suwarta., S.Th (West Java Regional Council Chairperson, nominated by that council). All three were declared eligible after a fit-and-proper test conducted by a panel formed by TPCP-GGP.

2. GGP General Assembly XV was originally scheduled for September 2020 in Manado, North Sulawesi, under TTG provisions. It was postponed for one year because of the worldwide COVID-19 pandemic, including in Indonesia. The Central Council issued Special Regulation (PERSUS) No. 03 of 2020, postponing council meetings, General Assembly XV, and auxiliary body deliberations, and extending the terms of Congregational, Area, Regional, and Central Councils, the Treasury Oversight Board (BPP), Board of Trustees, and auxiliary bodies of Gereja Gerekan Pentakosta during the pandemic.
B. General Assembly XV Proceedings

1. General Assembly XV was held on 22–23 October 2021 at Novotel Manado, North Sulawesi, in a hybrid format (onsite and online). Onsite attendance was limited to Central Council representatives (MHP and several officers), the Board of Trustees Chairperson and several members, Regional Council Chairpersons, and the organizing committee. Other eligible delegates from Regional, Area, and Congregational Councils across Indonesia participated and voted online from clusters in their respective regions.

Submission of General Chairperson candidate Pdt. Dicky Suwarta, S.Th's application documents by Pdt. Robertus Sela, M.Th (West Java GGP Regional Council Secretary) and Pdt. Sriyono, S.Pd.K (West Java GGP Area Council 4 Chairperson) to TPCP-GGP Chairperson Pdt. Yolla Pinaria, M.Th.

As a prospective General Chairperson for 2021–2026, Pdt. Dicky Suwarta, S.Th advocated the vision GGP IDAMAN KRISTUS (‘the Church Christ desires’), with the mission AIN Threefold: A = Advance, I = Influence, N = Next Level. ‘Threefold’ meant tripling GGP to 1,500 local churches over his five-year term. Seven parameters provided the basis for achieving this vision and mission:
1. Prioritizing church planting;
2. Productive GGP theology;
3. Sound teaching;
4. Structural integration;
5. Partnerships;
6. Up-to-date data;
7. Training young leaders.

2. The General Chairperson candidates formally approved by TPCP-GGP and confirmed by the assembly were Pdt. Dr. Welly Mamusung, M.Mis (number 1), Pdt. Dicky Suwarta, S.Th (number 2), and Pdt. Dr. Natanel Sunarno, M.Th (number 3). Each eligible participant voted via the Short Message System (SMS), sending a message to the Information Technology (IT) team appointed by the organizing committee. Pdt. Dicky Suwarta, S.Th was elected GGP General Chairperson for 2021–

2026. The presiding council then confirmed Pdt. Dicky Suwarta, S.Th as General Chairperson for 2021–2026. He proposed Pdm. Drs. Darmawan Soetedjo, MM as Board of Trustees (DP) Chairperson and Pdt. Sahaya Simbolon, SH as Treasury Oversight Board (BPP) Chairperson for 2021–2026; delegates accepted both proposals. He also proposed the following Central Executive Council (MHP) leadership: General Secretary: Pdt.
Robertus Sela, M.Th; General Treasurer: Pdm. Rudi; Chairperson 1: Pdt. Sularto, S.Th;

Chairperson 2: Pdt. Andreas Gunawan, M.Pd.K; Chairperson 3: Pdt. Hengly Mantak; Chairperson 4: Pdt. Ir, Karnada Margaka, M.Th. Delegates accepted these proposals and the presiding council confirmed them. Installation and ordination followed, with the decree read by General Assembly XV Secretary Pdt. Edmon Pakasi, M.Th. Senior GGP ministers appointed by the assembly then prayed and laid hands on the officers: Pdt. Dr. John Massie, M.Th; Pdt. Dr. Welly Mamusung, M.Mis; and Pdm. Yvonne AM. Makaminan, S.Th.
3. At the closing service on 23 October 2021, Pdt. Dicky Suwarta, S.Th was invited to preach from Haggai 2:20, with the sermon theme: ‘From this day on I will give blessings.’
Holy Communion was also celebrated at the closing service.
